introduction: The Spec Generation Improvement system adds splitting heuristics to the LLM task-generation prompt and validation warnings to the `afspec` validator, preventing oversized task groups that inflate session cost and degrade first-attempt quality.

glossary.ValidationError: An existing Pydantic model in `afspec/validation.py` representing a blocking diagnostic that causes validation to fail.
glossary.ValidationWarning: A Pydantic model in `afspec/validation.py` representing a non-blocking diagnostic produced during spec validation.
glossary.afspec: The Python package (`packages/afspec`) that provides spec validation logic, including the `validate()` function and the CLI command `spec validate`.
glossary.agentspec: The Python package (`packages/agentspec`) that contains prompt templates and spec generation utilities.
glossary.complexity weighting: A heuristic that assigns extra weight to subtasks involving multiple file changes, cross-module coordination, or intricate assertion patterns when deciding whether to split a group.
glossary.generation_user_tasks.md: The Markdown prompt template in `packages/agentspec/agentspec/_templates/prompts/` that instructs the LLM how to generate tasks.json for a spec.
glossary.group_id: The integer identifier of a task group within tasks.json, used as a prefix in subtask IDs (e.g. group 1 → subtask 1.2).
glossary.kind: The category of a task group; valid values are `tests`, `standard`, and `checkpoint`.
glossary.spec 07: The `nightshift_standalone_cli` spec, the motivating example of an oversized task group that required three costly coder→audit cycles.
glossary.spec validate: The CLI command provided by `afspec` that validates a spec file and reports errors and warnings.
glossary.splitting: The process of dividing an oversized task group into two or more smaller groups during spec generation, each staying within defined thresholds.
glossary.subtask: A numbered unit of work within a task group, identified by `{group_id}.{N}` (e.g. 1.2), excluding the verification subtask.
glossary.task group: A logical unit of work in a spec's tasks.json that maps 1:1 to a single coder session; contains subtasks and a verification subtask.
glossary.tasks.json: The JSON artifact produced by the LLM (via `agentspec`) that describes the task groups and subtasks for a spec.
glossary.test spec entries: Individual test-case identifiers (e.g. `TS-08-1`) listed in a subtask's `test_spec_refs` array.
glossary.test_spec_refs: The list of test-spec entry IDs referenced by a subtask, used to measure the test coverage scope a subtask imposes on a session.
glossary.verification subtask: The final subtask in a task group, identified by `{group_id}.V`, containing checks that verify all other subtasks in the group.

requirements.title: Prompt splitting rule — test spec ref ceiling

user_story.goal: have the LLM automatically split any task group that would reference more than 15 test spec entries across its subtasks
user_story.benefit: each resulting coder session stays within a manageable scope and produces higher-quality output on the first attempt

acceptance_criteria.action: instructs the LLM that if the total count of `test_spec_refs` across all subtasks in a proposed task group exceeds 15, the group must be split into smaller groups each containing 15 or fewer `test_spec_refs`
applies the 15 `test_spec_refs` ceiling rule to all `kind` values (`tests`, `standard`, `checkpoint`), not only `kind: tests` groups
produces task groups where no single group's total `test_spec_refs` count across all subtasks exceeds 15
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: tasks.json where every group satisfies the ceiling constraint
acceptance_criteria.trigger: the LLM generates `tasks.json` for any spec

edge_cases.action: does not split the group solely based on this rule; other rules may still apply
edge_cases.error_condition: a spec has so few test spec entries that all subtasks collectively reference ≤ 15 entries

requirements.title: Prompt splitting rule — subtask count ceiling

user_story.goal: have the LLM keep each task group to at most 6 subtasks (excluding the verification subtask)
user_story.benefit: sessions remain focused and reviewable within a single cycle

acceptance_criteria.action: instructs the LLM that if a task group would exceed 6 subtasks (excluding the `verification subtask`), it must be split into smaller groups
applies the 6-subtask ceiling to all `kind` values (`tests`, `standard`, `checkpoint`)
produces task groups where no single group contains more than 6 subtasks (the `verification subtask` is excluded from this count)
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: tasks.json where every group's subtask count (excluding `verification subtask`) is ≤ 6
acceptance_criteria.trigger: the LLM generates `tasks.json` for any spec

edge_cases.action: does not split the group based on subtask count alone
edge_cases.error_condition: a group has exactly 6 subtasks and no other threshold is exceeded

user_story.goal: have the LLM recognize that subtasks with complex logic impose heavier session load even if numeric counts are low
user_story.benefit: groups containing high-complexity work are split proactively, avoiding expensive retry cycles

acceptance_criteria.action: defines `complexity weighting` as: a subtask is complex if it involves multiple file changes, cross-module coordination, or intricate assertion patterns, and instructs the LLM to split a group with 4 or more complex subtasks even when numeric thresholds are not exceeded
splits the group regardless of whether the `test_spec_refs` count or subtask count ceiling has been reached
acceptance_criteria.trigger: the LLM identifies 4 or more complex subtasks in a proposed task group

edge_cases.action: does not split based on `complexity weighting` alone; the group is retained as-is
edge_cases.error_condition: a group has 3 complex subtasks and no numeric threshold is exceeded

requirements.title: Prompt splitting strategy — group by requirement

user_story.goal: have the LLM group related subtasks together when splitting
user_story.benefit: each resulting task group covers a cohesive functional area, making sessions easier to review and audit

acceptance_criteria.action: instructs the LLM that when splitting a task group, subtasks must be grouped by the requirement they trace to, so that each resulting group covers a distinct set of requirements

instructs the LLM that when a `kind: tests` group is split, all resulting groups retain `kind: tests`, the first split group retains `group_id` 1, and subsequent groups receive sequential IDs (2, 3, …)
instructs the LLM that non-test groups shift their IDs to follow the last test group, and that subtask IDs within each group use the `{group_id}.{N}` format

edge_cases.action: splits the group by further subdividing that requirement's subtasks across multiple groups, each staying within thresholds
edge_cases.error_condition: subtasks in a group all trace to the same single requirement but still exceed a numeric threshold

requirements.title: Validation warning — oversized test spec refs per group

user_story.goal: receive a warning when I run `spec validate` on a spec whose task group totals more than 15 `test_spec_refs`
user_story.benefit: I can catch oversized groups before they are executed and incur high session costs

acceptance_criteria.action: emits a `ValidationWarning` identifying the offending group and the actual count
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: validation result with `valid: true` and at least one `ValidationWarning` entry
acceptance_criteria.trigger: `spec validate` is run on a spec where a task group's total `test_spec_refs` count across all its subtasks exceeds 15

acceptance_criteria.action: applies the oversized `test_spec_refs` check to all task groups regardless of `kind`
does not emit a `ValidationWarning` for that group based on this rule
acceptance_criteria.state: a task group's total `test_spec_refs` count is exactly 15 or fewer

edge_cases.action: treats the count as zero and does not emit a `ValidationWarning` for the `test_spec_refs` rule
edge_cases.error_condition: a task group has no subtasks or no `test_spec_refs` defined

requirements.title: Validation warning — too many subtasks per group

user_story.goal: receive a warning when a task group contains more than 6 subtasks
user_story.benefit: I can identify groups that will produce oversized sessions before they run

acceptance_criteria.action: emits a `ValidationWarning` identifying the offending group and the actual subtask count
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: validation result with `valid: true` and at least one `ValidationWarning` entry
acceptance_criteria.trigger: `spec validate` is run on a spec where a task group contains more than 6 subtasks (excluding the `verification subtask`)

acceptance_criteria.action: excludes the `verification subtask` from the subtask count when evaluating this rule
does not emit a `ValidationWarning` for that group based on this rule
acceptance_criteria.state: a task group has exactly 6 or fewer subtasks (excluding the `verification subtask`)

edge_cases.action: emits exactly one `ValidationWarning` for the too-many-subtasks rule for that group
edge_cases.return_contract: validation result with `valid: true` and one `ValidationWarning` for the group
edge_cases.error_condition: a task group has exactly 7 subtasks excluding the `verification subtask`

user_story.goal: receive a warning when a single subtask references more than 8 test spec entries
user_story.benefit: I can spot individual subtasks that are over-scoped and may dominate a session

acceptance_criteria.action: emits a `ValidationWarning` identifying the offending subtask ID and the actual count
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: validation result with `valid: true` and at least one `ValidationWarning` entry
acceptance_criteria.trigger: `spec validate` is run on a spec where any subtask references more than 8 `test_spec_refs`

acceptance_criteria.action: does not emit a `ValidationWarning` for that subtask based on this rule
acceptance_criteria.state: a subtask references exactly 8 or fewer `test_spec_refs`

edge_cases.action: treats the count as zero and does not emit a `ValidationWarning` for that subtask
edge_cases.error_condition: a subtask has no `test_spec_refs` field or an empty list

requirements.title: ValidationWarning model and updated validate() return contract

user_story.goal: have a distinct `ValidationWarning` model returned alongside errors from `validate()`
user_story.benefit: I can programmatically distinguish non-blocking diagnostics from blocking errors

acceptance_criteria.action: defines a `ValidationWarning` Pydantic model in `afspec/validation.py` with at minimum fields for the warning message and the offending entity identifier
updates `validate()` to return both a list of `ValidationError` objects and a list of `ValidationWarning` objects
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: tuple or structured result containing `errors: list[ValidationError]` and `warnings: list[ValidationWarning]`

acceptance_criteria.action: reports `valid: true` in its return value
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: result with `valid: true`, empty `errors` list, and non-empty `warnings` list
acceptance_criteria.state: the `validate()` function produces only `ValidationWarning` objects and no `ValidationError` objects

edge_cases.action: returns `valid: false` with both the errors and warnings lists populated
edge_cases.return_contract: result with `valid: false`, non-empty `errors` list, and non-empty `warnings` list
edge_cases.condition: when a spec triggers both `ValidationError` and `ValidationWarning` conditions

user_story.goal: see validation warnings printed in the `spec validate` CLI output
user_story.benefit: I am informed of potential sizing issues without being blocked from continuing

acceptance_criteria.action: displays each warning message to the user and prints a final `valid: true` status
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: exit code 0, stdout contains warning messages and 'valid: true'
acceptance_criteria.trigger: `spec validate` completes with one or more `ValidationWarning` objects and no errors

acceptance_criteria.action: displays no warning messages and prints a final `valid: true` status
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: exit code 0, stdout contains 'valid: true' with no warning lines
acceptance_criteria.trigger: `spec validate` completes with no errors and no warnings

acceptance_criteria.action: displays all errors and warnings and prints `valid: false`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: non-zero exit code, stdout/stderr contains error and warning messages and 'valid: false'
acceptance_criteria.trigger: `spec validate` completes with one or more `ValidationError` objects alongside any number of `ValidationWarning` objects

edge_cases.action: reports a parse error as a `ValidationError` (not a `ValidationWarning`) and exits with a non-zero code
edge_cases.return_contract: non-zero exit code, error message indicating parse failure
edge_cases.error_condition: the spec file cannot be parsed at all

user_story.goal: have all pre-existing validation rules continue to work after this change
user_story.benefit: I do not need to update existing valid specs when the new warnings are introduced

acceptance_criteria.action: continues to enforce the rule that `groups[0].kind` must equal `tests`, unchanged by the addition of `ValidationWarning` logic
allows multiple consecutive task groups with `kind: tests` without emitting a `ValidationError`, as this was already permitted

correctness_properties.title: Warnings never block validity
correctness_properties.invariant: if `validate()` returns zero `ValidationError` objects, the result's `valid` field is `true` regardless of how many `ValidationWarning` objects are present

correctness_properties.title: Oversized group always warned
correctness_properties.for_any: task group where total `test_spec_refs` count across all subtasks exceeds 15
correctness_properties.invariant: `afspec` emits at least one `ValidationWarning` referencing that group when `spec validate` is run

correctness_properties.title: Subtask overload always warned
correctness_properties.for_any: task group where the number of subtasks excluding the `verification subtask` exceeds 6
correctness_properties.invariant: `afspec` emits at least one `ValidationWarning` referencing that group when `spec validate` is run

correctness_properties.title: Single subtask overload always warned
correctness_properties.invariant: `afspec` emits at least one `ValidationWarning` referencing that subtask when `spec validate` is run

correctness_properties.title: LLM-generated groups respect thresholds
correctness_properties.for_any: task group in a `tasks.json` produced by the LLM using the updated `generation_user_tasks.md`
correctness_properties.invariant: the group's total `test_spec_refs` count across all subtasks is ≤ 15 and the group's subtask count (excluding the `verification subtask`) is ≤ 6

execution_paths.title: LLM generates tasks.json with oversized group — splitting applied

steps.action: triggers spec generation for a large spec with many requirements and test spec entries
loads `generation_user_tasks.md` and includes it in the LLM prompt
detects that a proposed task group would exceed 15 `test_spec_refs` or 6 subtasks and applies `splitting` guided by the prompt rules
groups subtasks by the requirement they trace to, assigns sequential `group_id` values, and formats subtask IDs using `{group_id}.{N}`
writes the resulting `tasks.json` where all groups satisfy the size thresholds

execution_paths.title: spec validate — warnings only, valid result

steps.action: runs `spec validate` on a spec whose `tasks.json` contains a task group with 20 total `test_spec_refs`
parses the spec and evaluates all validation rules including the new size-threshold checks
finds no `ValidationError` conditions but detects the oversized group and constructs one or more `ValidationWarning` objects
prints each `ValidationWarning` message to stdout and reports `valid: true` with exit code 0

execution_paths.title: spec validate — errors and warnings, invalid result

steps.action: runs `spec validate` on a spec with a structural error (e.g. missing required field) and an oversized task group
parses the spec and evaluates all validation rules
produces both a `ValidationError` for the structural issue and a `ValidationWarning` for the oversized group
prints all errors and warnings, reports `valid: false`, and exits with a non-zero code

execution_paths.title: spec validate — clean spec, no warnings

steps.action: runs `spec validate` on a spec where all task groups are within size thresholds and no structural errors exist
evaluates all validation rules and finds neither errors nor warnings
prints `valid: true` with exit code 0 and no warning output

error_handling.condition: A task group's total `test_spec_refs` count across all subtasks exceeds 15 in a spec passed to `spec validate`
error_handling.behavior: afspec emits a `ValidationWarning` (not a `ValidationError`); validation continues and returns `valid: true` if no errors are present

error_handling.condition: A task group contains more than 6 subtasks (excluding the `verification subtask`) in a spec passed to `spec validate`
error_handling.behavior: afspec emits a `ValidationWarning`; validation continues and returns `valid: true` if no errors are present

error_handling.condition: A subtask references more than 8 `test_spec_refs` in a spec passed to `spec validate`
error_handling.behavior: afspec emits a `ValidationWarning` identifying the subtask; validation continues and returns `valid: true` if no errors are present

error_handling.condition: Both `ValidationError` and `ValidationWarning` conditions are present in the same spec
error_handling.behavior: afspec returns `valid: false` with all errors and warnings populated; the CLI displays both and exits with a non-zero code

error_handling.condition: The spec file cannot be parsed (e.g. malformed YAML/JSON)
error_handling.behavior: afspec raises or returns a `ValidationError` for the parse failure; no warnings are emitted; CLI exits with a non-zero code
